page: Amazon Web Services x8g.12xlarge is a memory-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro system and driven by 48 physical ARM Neoverse-V2 cores running at 2.8 GHz. The architecture uses dedicated single-threaded cores without simultaneous multithreading, ensuring consistent execution across all vCPUs. It is provisioned with 768.0 GB of system memory, establishing a 1:16 vCPU-to-memory ratio with 16.0 GB of RAM allocated per core. The instance includes no onboard local storage and no GPU accelerators, using network-attached volumes for persistent data alongside a 22 Gbps baseline network interface.

Benchmark results highlight an exceptionally capable memory subsystem and strong parallel computing capacity. Large-block uncached memory read bandwidth reached 368.85 GB/sec and write bandwidth reached 186.53 GB/sec, placing the instance in the top decile of tested systems. Multi-core performance is similarly robust, highlighted by a Geekbench multi-core score of 23349.0, a Clang compilation score of 69875.0, and a stress-ng multi-core result of 81892.57. Conversely, single-core processing metrics remain in the middle tier, with Geekbench single-core scoring 1764.0 and stress-ng single-core scoring 1706.89.

The x8g.12xlarge offers qualitative cost efficiency for organizations requiring high RAM density per compute unit, driven by the power and packaging efficiencies of the Graviton platform. In tests focused on data operations, the instance produced 99.15 million Redis SET operations per second and achieved top-tier marks in database throughput. The primary architectural tradeoff is the complete absence of integrated NVMe storage, meaning that disk-heavy workloads rely entirely on network storage performance. This instance is best configured for large in-memory databases, Redis caches, distributed in-memory data processing, and large-footprint analytical workloads.
description: Amazon Web Services x8g.12xlarge is a memory-optimized cloud instance powered by 48 dedicated physical arm64 cores based on AWS Graviton Neoverse-V2 architecture running at 2.8 GHz. Configured without simultaneous multithreading, it provides 768.0 GB of system memory, equating to 16.0 GB per core, along with a 22 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. The instance features no local storage or onboard GPUs, relying on external block storage. Benchmark results show top-tier memory bandwidth, reaching 368.85 GB/sec for large-block uncached reads and 186.53 GB/sec for writes, coupled with top-tier multi-threaded compilation and database operations. While single-thread execution is in the middle 50%, multi-core throughput is strong, generating 99.15 million Redis SET operations per second. The x8g.12xlarge is architected for large-scale in-memory databases, in-memory caching, real-time analytics, and memory-bound multi-threaded workloads.
